paper_title: Frog in the Pan: Continuous Information and Momentum
selected_experiment: Table 2, Panel A: sequential double-sorts on formation-period return (PRET) quintiles, then information discreteness (ID) quintiles; six-month momentum (winner minus loser) by ID quintile after skipping one month, post-1927 sample

economic_rationale.value: Frog-in-the-pan (limited attention): investors are inattentive to information arriving continuously in small amounts and process it with a delay, so continuous information produces stronger, more persistent return continuation than discrete information

evidence.quote: We test a frog-in-the-pan (FIP) hypothesis that predicts investors are inattentive to information arriving continuously in small amounts.

universe_and_filters.value: CRSP stocks (returns adjusted for delistings), 1927 to 2007 sample, with a $5 price filter imposed at the beginning of each month

evidence.quote: Speciﬁcally, after imposing a $5 price ﬁlter at the beginning of each month, we sort stocks into quintiles according to their PRET and then subdivide these quintiles into ID subportfolios.

value: cumulative stock returns over the formation period (PRET)

evidence.quote: We obtain return data from the Center for Research in Security Prices (CRSP) after adjusting for delistings and ﬁrm-level accounting data from COMPUSTA T.

signal_formula_words.value: Information discreteness (ID): the sign of the formation-period return PRET times the difference between the percentage of formation-period days with negative daily returns and the percentage with positive daily returns; low ID means continuous information, high ID means discrete information; stocks are first sorted on PRET, then on ID

evidence.quote: Our benchmark ID proxy is determined by the sign of daily returns and ignores their magnitude by equally weighting each observed return.

signal_formula_symbols.value: ID = sgn(PRET) × [%neg − %pos], where PRET is the cumulative formation-period return and %pos, %neg are the percentages of formation-period days with positive and negative returns

formation_window.value: 12 months of daily returns (past twelve months, skipping the most recent month)

evidence.quote: Speciﬁcally, PRET is deﬁned as a ﬁrm’s cumulative return over the past twelve months after skipping the most recent month.
Post-formation momentum returns over six months, deﬁned as the return from buying winners and selling losers, are reported for each ID quintile after skipping one intermediate month.
Post-formation returns over the next six months and three years are then computed.
Momentum proﬁts in month t +x, where x ranges from 1 to 10, based on double-sorted portfolios formed in month t according to formation- period returns and ID.

sort_rule_evidence.quote: The results in Panel A pertain to sequential double-sorts involving PRET quintiles, then ID quintiles.

breakpoints.value: sequential: quintiles of PRET, then ID quintiles within the PRET quintiles; breakpoint universe (all stocks vs NYSE) not stated

evidence.quote: we sort stocks into quintiles according to their PRET and then subdivide these quintiles into ID subportfolios

favored_group.value: momentum (past winners minus past losers) within the lowest ID (continuous information) quintile

evidence.quote: decreases monotonically from 5.94% in the low ID quintile containing stocks with continuous information to –2.07% in the high ID quintile containing stocks with discrete information

disfavored_group.value: momentum (past winners minus past losers) within the highest ID (discrete information) quintile

evidence.quote: decreases monotonically from 5.94% in the low ID quintile containing stocks with continuous information to –2.07% in the high ID quintile containing stocks with discrete information

weighting_evidence.quote: momentum, the six-month return from buying winners and selling losers

expected_sign_evidence.quote: Consistent with the FIP hypothesis, continuous information induces stronger and more persistent return continuation than discrete information after conditioning on the magnitude of formation-period returns.

headline_result.value: Six-month momentum of 5.94% in the continuous (low ID) quintile vs –2.07% in the discrete (high ID) quintile; difference 8.01% (t-statistic 8.54), post-1927

evidence.quote: This 8.01% difference in momentum has a t-statistic of 8.54 during the post-1927 sample period.

unresolved_details: Portfolio weighting (equal vs value) within the double-sorted portfolios is not stated; weighting recorded as 'other' (not stated).
Breakpoint universe for PRET and ID quintiles (all stocks vs NYSE) is not stated.
Whether six-month holding periods overlap (Jegadeesh-Titman style overlapping portfolios) or how monthly cohorts are combined is not stated.
Exact formation window endpoints ('past twelve months after skipping the most recent month': whether 12 or 11 months of returns, e.g. t-12 to t-2) are not spelled out.
Return convention for the six-month holding-period return (compounded vs summed monthly returns) is not stated.
Treatment of PRET exactly equal to zero (sgn defined only for PRET > 0 and PRET < 0) is not stated.
Minimum number of daily return observations required to compute ID is not stated.
Share-code, exchange, or other universe filters beyond the $5 price filter are not stated.
Section 1 says negative book values are eliminated from the sample (Compustat data); whether this filter applies to the 1927-2007 Table 2 sorts is not stated.
Which price is used for the $5 filter (price at beginning of month, i.e. end of prior month) is only loosely specified.
